subject: Post-demo questions: region pinning, backups, and logging controls (MedBridge)
messages:
From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@medbridge.io>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: region pinning & backup questions (MedBridge)

Hi Rishi / Ben / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — it helped our engineering and compliance teams understand Redwood's hosting options. We have a short list of follow-up items on residency, backups, and logs so we can map to our privacy controls. Can you confirm the following at a high level and call out any constraints?

1) Region pinning: We need customer PII (names, contact info, health identifiers) to remain physically stored only in EU data centers. Is it possible to pin an entire account's production dataset to EU with zero-copy backups outside EU?

2) Cross-region failover: We require a failover plan that does not violate data sovereignty. If EU primary fails, can Redwood failover to a warm-standby in the US while ensuring PII is not replicated to the US? If not, what alternative patterns do you support (e.g., metadata-only warm standby, tokenized proxies)?

3) Backups & snapshots: What's your snapshot replication policy? Can we limit snapshot replication target regions? What are the typical RPO/RTO numbers for snapshot restore in the EU region?

4) Logging and telemetry: We need audit logs for API requests and model outputs for 12 months. Can logs that may contain PII be redacted or sent to a customer-controlled KMS/Log archive in EU only? How do you handle model-generated data that may contain sensitive content?

5) Encryption & KMS: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMEK) with EU key storage (e.g., KMS in eu-west-1)? If CMEK is used, are snapshots and backups encrypted with the same key and kept in-region?

6) Compliance docs: We will need SOC 2 Type II report, current DPA language, and an entry-level residency appendix to include in our security review. Can you share these or confirm availability?

I've attached a small data map and a spreadsheet with our minimal retention requirements. Please let me know if you'd like to schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra team.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, IT Security
MedBridge

Subject: Re: Post-demo: region pinning & backup questions (MedBridge)

Hi Elena — great questions, and thanks for the clear data map. Short answers up front, followed by a suggested set of next steps.

1) Region pinning: Yes — we support account- and route-level pinning. For your use case we can pin production datasets and associated KV/prefix caches to EU-only storage and compute. That pin prevents automatic replication to other regions.

2) Cross-region failover: We offer multiple failover patterns:
  - EU-primary (recommended): compute + storage pinned to EU. Optional warm-standby in another region that holds *metadata only* (healthchecks, routing state), not customer PII.
  - Active-active variant is possible for non-PII workloads.
  - Emergency failover (manual): on an agreed process we can restore EU snapshot into a compliant environment in another region, but that requires explicit approval and contract-level authorization.

3) Backups & snapshots: Snapshots are configurable. Default behavior is local-region snapshots; we can disable cross-region snapshot replication. Typical EU restore times (RTO) are 30–90 minutes for small data sets, RPO depends on snapshot cadence — we can do sub-hourly snapshots if required.

4) Logging and telemetry: Audit logs can be exported to a customer-controlled log sink (S3/Blob) in EU. We support server-side redaction rules and token-level sampling to reduce PII in logs. Model outputs that contain user PII can be routed to the customer's retention bucket; retention policies are configurable.

5) Encryption & KMS: We support CMEK — keys can be hosted in EU KMS. Snapshots and backups are encrypted with the configured CMEK, and we can block snapshot exports unless the export target is EU.

6) Compliance docs: SOC 2 Type II summary and our standard DPA are available; I'll attach a residency quicksheet with implementation notes.

Next steps I propose:
  - I will share a residency appendix + quicksheet (attached).
  - Please fill our short residency questionnaire so we can size storage and replication needs: https://forms.gle/medbridge-residency-qs
  - Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (Ben) to walk through the snapshot/export controls and CMEK key bindings.

Attaching: redwood-residency-quicksheet.pdf (high-level implementation notes).

Happy to hop on a call tomorrow or early next week.

Best,

On Thu, Jul 11, 2029 at 12:02 PM, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai wrote:
> 1) Region pinning: Yes — we support account- and route-level pinning. For your use case we can pin production datasets and associated KV/prefix caches to EU-only storage and compute.

Quick internal notes / proposal:
- For MedBridge, propose EU-primary with a metadata-only warm standby in us-west for routing and health checks. That lets them failover traffic to an endpoint that returns 503 + maintenance page rather than returning PII-laden results, until an approved EU restore occurs.
- Snapshot policy: set hourly incremental snapshots with daily full snapshot. Disable automatic cross-region replication; add manual export workflow with approval ticket.
- Logging: push full audit stream to customer-owned EU S3, use redact rules on server side for tokens and direct PII.

Open question for Monica: if they require DR that allows automatic traffic failover to the US (i.e., to continue serving queries against data), how do we want to phrase the contractual restriction and approval flow? We should make it visible in the residency appendix and require signed authorization for any cross-border restore.

Ben
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Elena — following internal alignment (Ben/Monica looped in), here is a consolidated plan and concrete next steps: 

Plan (what Redwood will commit to in a standard Dedicated/Private deployment):
- EU-primary pin: production compute and storage (including KV caches) remain in EU. No automatic snapshot replication outside EU by default.
- Warm-standby pattern: metadata-only warm standby in US is available for routing and failover signalling; it intentionally does not contain PII.
- Manual cross-border restore: in an emergency we will perform a restore into a non-EU region only after written customer authorization and completion of the cross-border restore request ticket. This will be documented in the residency appendix and addendum.
- Snapshots: hourly incremental / daily full (configurable). By default snapshots are stored in EU; exports are blocked unless approved.
- KMS & encryption: CMEK supported. Keys can be in eu-west KMS and used for encryption of snapshots/backups.
- Logging: full audit stream delivered to customer-owned EU bucket; server-side redaction available. Retention configurable up to 24 months.

Action items:
1) Elena/MedBridge: complete the residency questionnaire here: https://forms.gle/medbridge-residency-qs (this helps us size and produce an appendix).
2) Redwood: share residency appendix + SOC 2 summary (link above). I'll drop the appendix to the shared link: https://redwood.app/s/RESIDENCY-APPENDIX-MDB-2029
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive (Ben + Monica) next week to walk replicas, snapshot export control, and CMEK binding. Proposed times: Mon 15 Jul 9–11am PT or Tue 16 Jul 1–3pm PT. Tell us which works for your infra lead.

If this looks good I will send a calendar invite and attach the residency appendix as a draft.

Thanks again — looking forward to the deep-dive.
